Changelog

Builds are numbered; the package identity is FM-1_7 and the build in 2 digits (build 3: FM-1_703).

Build 3 — November 2026

The 1st public build. The Pulsar-23 recreated as a whole instrument, then pushed toward experimental IDM.

  • Engine. Every module of the Pulsar-23 modelled on its 0–10 V scale: clock and divider array, 4 looper-recorders, envelopes, BD, BASS, SD, HHT, SHAOS, LFO, the FX processor, the parallel distortion, VCAs, inverters, switches, attenuators, pulse converters, MIDI-CV and touch CV, noise, a diode and 2 capacitors, and a virtual patchbay of 32 cables. Fixed-point throughout, rendered on both of the FM-1's cores.
  • 16 engine profiles. The 4 circuits in 16 modes: BD, HAMMER, SKIN; SD, WALL, WIRE, TONE; HHT, STATIC, METAL, SHAKE; GRIND, BASS, FM, PRC, PLUCK. Pitch from the note played (no TUNE).
  • Sounds. 147 families drawn at random, all percussive; 4 macros on the main knobs; 4 internal routes per sound (SHAOS, the LFO, the dividers, noise, FX outputs, any track's output or envelope); a per-voice drive; WRECK (fold, ring, crush, bits) after every voice.
  • STUTTER on the 6th black key, apart from the FX: SHIFT and the key held repeat the slice just heard; its page has SLICE, RATE, MODE, DECAY (each with RND), DRIFT, ROLL and MIX. The key is lit dimly.
  • BREAK has 10 ways (REPEAT, HALF TIME, DOUBLE, REVERSE, CHOP, ROLL, SHUFFLE, POLY, JUMP, SKIP) and layers drawn at random: ratchets up to 8, octave leaps, flams, accents, RISE, WRECK, STUT, GHOST. Nothing drops out.
  • Phrases: polymeters, tracks on their own clock and direction, crossed Euclidean layers, ratchets, hits late or graced, walking velocities; their locks reach WRECK.
  • PERFORMANCE on the 7th black key: the state kept, everything changed put back as it goes off; the main knobs move every track with notes (CTRL ALL). Each session's CTRL sets KNOBS or ALL (phrases, locks, directions, lengths, clocks, transposition, new sounds and EDIT pages on every track). A pattern saved while it is on keeps what plays, and the sounds of that moment stay in the session.
  • Sessions on a grid like the patterns': a white key loads its session, held it saves there.
  • The pages Quasar cannot use without cables (CLOCK, LOOPER, ATTEN, CV, PATCH) are hidden; the clock follows the session tempo.
  • The output is written at full scale into a soft clip: Quasar is loud.

Builds 1 and 2 — October 2026

Development builds, not published. Build 1 joined Pulsar-23 circuits to the Bigorna engine and was withdrawn; build 2 replaced it with an independent engine (per-track circuits, 4 fixed modulation cables), which build 3 replaced in turn.

Developed by Nuno Zimas. Firmware: GPL-3.0. Website and logo: MIT. Source on GitHub.
